comment: The DeepSeek Harness version line this plugin pack is built and tested against. Plugins are shipped as alpha until the owner promotes them to stable. The installer pins this exact dsh version when driving the CLI. 'vendoredFrom' records the harness line whose client bundles dsh-rightbar / dsh-rightbar-files / dsh-open-in-app were forked from. dsh-vn-master is the pack's master: the bundle layer alone - the pack's final word per row, no browser half.
comment_platforms: The plugins are plain JavaScript and platform-neutral; the only OS-specific code is a launcher choosing the right command for the host: dsh-open-in-app's file-browser launcher (explorer.exe / open / xdg-open, WSL-aware), the run launcher's browser hand-off (Chrome on PATH / the standard install folders / the App Paths registry entry, 'open -a Google Chrome', google-chrome or chromium, else the platform default). The launchers run on Windows (install.bat / uninstall.bat, PowerShell 5.1 or 7, and the run launcher: the double-clickable batch run-web.bat at the root plus its worker scripts/run-web.ps1, because cmd's for /f reads a child's output only up to EOF and cannot watch a running harness) and on macOS/Linux (install.sh / uninstall.sh / run-web.sh, POSIX sh - never PowerShell). The run launcher is run-web.bat + run-web.sh at the repo root, and run-web.sh does the whole job itself. The ready URL reaches the browser as ONE ARGV ELEMENT - Start-Process -ArgumentList on Windows, an argument of open/xdg-open on macOS/Linux - never through a command string.

dsh-vn-master.role: Master: the pack base bundle and its final profile layer - it installs last, so a later layer wins per row, and it adds one no-op `master` host row. It carries the pack-wide row decisions: the four feedback/telemetry rows are disabled, and the pack's own `browser` row is disabled too (built and shipped, deliberately off). See packages/dsh-vn-master/README.md.

dsh-rightbar.role: Right bar: the tab strip, docking panel, expand button, Start page and the `sidebarRightTabs` / `sidebarRight` services every tab type registers into. A GENERATED fork of the shipped bar whose layer disables `ui-sidebar-right` / `ui-sidebar-files`, rendering the kit's recursive `DockSurface` through its own `vendor/dock-tree.js`. See packages/dsh-rightbar/README.md.

dsh-editor.role: Editor: the tab type for text and code - a vendored CodeMirror 6 fetched lazily - with create-on-save inside the session workspace through this package's own authenticated routes. Markdown is claimed too, and hands off to the shipped preview. See packages/dsh-editor/README.md.

shadowsSlots.why: the rendered Markdown body carries the Edit toggle back into the editor (lower priority renders) and undoes what the preview's plain-text scrollport imposes on its contents (white-space:pre and the mono font stack)

dsh-gittree.role: History: a read-only tab showing the workspace's commit graph, each commit's message and the files it touched. Three read-only routes spawn `git` with argv arrays under a pinned env; nothing here can write, stage or check out. See packages/dsh-gittree/README.md.

dsh-image.role: Image: a viewer tab for PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP/AVIF/BMP/ICO/SVG/TIFF that fits the pane on open, zooms by moving the LAYOUT (never a transform), pans by drag and reads the pixel under the pointer. Client-only: the bytes come from the harness's own `remote.workspaceFiles`. See packages/dsh-image/README.md.

dsh-audio.role: Audio: WAV/AIFF/FLAC as a waveform - one row per channel, an adaptive ruler, a min/max envelope with the RMS core, zoom down to samples, selection, and playback on the audio clock - plus the Audio console for this machine's devices. Client-only, read in 2 MiB windows. See packages/dsh-audio/README.md.
uses: dsh-modal (the pack's shared dialog surface: the console's seat opens it lazily through ctx.get and never injects it, so a profile without it draws the console inline as a page instead)
@deepseek-ai/dsh-api-workspace-files (the workspaceFiles remote: readBytes windows, readAll, stat)

dsh-media.role: The pack's media engine and the only owner of ffmpeg (host-only, no browser half): `media_probe`, `media_run` and `media_frames`, the Range-capable file route, remux jobs, and the pinned hash-verified ffmpeg provisioning that dsh-video's tab streams through. See packages/dsh-media/README.md.
uses: the host's own `tar` for unpacking a pinned archive
optional (only when provisioning): the pinned static builds from BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds and evermeet.cx
vendors: NOT a vendored engine: lib/binaries.json is a PIN (official URL + SHA-256 per platform-arch) whose bytes are downloaded to $DSH_HOME/dsh-media/bin only on a machine with no ffmpeg of its own (BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds autobuild-2026-09-26-13-03 for win32/linux, evermeet.cx 9.0.2 for darwin-x64)

dsh-video.role: Video: a player tab for MP4/MOV/WebM/MKV/AVI/WMV/FLV/OGV/TS/3GP that fits the pane, with the ffprobe facts, chapters as jump targets and one-click remux/convert. The bytes never enter the tab: the `<video>` is handed a URL to dsh-media's Range route. See packages/dsh-video/README.md.
uses: dsh-rightbar (the tab registry and the keyed pane seats)
dsh-media (the file/report/remux/job routes and the ffmpeg behind them - resolved over HTTP, so a profile without it still loads and says so)

dsh-browser.role: Browser: the pack's own web surface, which fetches and renders a page on the HOST in a disposable sandboxed engine behind an egress gate instead of framing it remotely - three tools and three routes. Currently disabled by dsh-vn-master's `browser` row; re-enabling it is deleting those two lines. See packages/dsh-browser/README.md.

dsh-diagrams.role: Diagrams: Mermaid and TikZ in one bundle - six `diagram_*` tools whose writes are validated on the host before they are stored, a conversation store plus a shared library, a tab per diagram with an export menu, an index page, and browser render reports. See packages/dsh-diagrams/README.md.
uses: a TeX engine on PATH (pdflatex/xelatex/lualatex) for TikZ
vendors: the two skills copied into $DSH_HOME/skills by both installers

dsh-pdf.role: PDF: five `pdf_*` tools (info, read, find, render, scan) over a vendored pdf.js, plus the reader tab (zoom, search, thumbnails, outline) and a workspace index. Read-only, with extraction in a child process that never evaluates a document's JavaScript. See packages/dsh-pdf/README.md.
uses: optional: poppler pdftoppm / mutool / Ghostscript for pdf_render and pdf_scan, tesseract (+ language data) for OCR
vendors: pdfjs-dist@6.3.289 (lib/vendor/pdf.min.mjs + pdf.worker.min.mjs + cmaps/ + standard_fonts/ + wasm/ + LICENSE, GENERATED by vendor/build.mjs; VERSION.json records every file's bytes+sha256 and a digest per tree, --check re-hashes it offline, and .gitattributes pins its text files to LF)
the pdf-analysis skill copied into $DSH_HOME/skills by both installers

dsh-cmdbar.role: Command bar: a read-only transcript of the agent's own commands in a bottom dock, fed by one bounded read-only route. One view, and no shell of its own. See packages/dsh-cmdbar/README.md.

dsh-modal.role: Modal: the pack's shared dialog surface, published as the `modals` service - `open` / `alert` / `confirm` / `prompt` with async submit work that keeps the dialog open, plus a rich `content` dialog whose mask click deliberately does not close it. See packages/dsh-modal/README.md.

uses: @deepseek-ai/dsh-skill (ctx.skills, the host skill registry - NOT injected, resolved lazily per request)
dsh-modal (the shared dialog surface, opened in its rich `content` form; resolved lazily so a profile without it still loads)
dsh-skills.role: Skills browser: one header seat opens a modal listing every skill the harness loads for this conversation, with three routes to read and save the markdown behind it. The client names a skill, never a path. See packages/dsh-skills/README.md.

owns: the profile's own Cordis patch -> the `ui-state` entry's `config` (pageZoom, theme, dockHeight, sidebarWidth, rightbarWidth), through the five `.volatile()` fields this row declares
dsh-ui-state.role: UI state that outlives the process: the page zoom, an extension theme, the dock height and the two column widths, kept in one durable settings section and applied before first paint for the zoom. See packages/dsh-ui-state/README.md.

uses: dsh-ui-state (the uiState service, resolved lazily through ctx.get, for the durable page zoom and extension theme)
dsh-themes.role: Themes and header dress: the conversation header's own controls (page zoom, Screenshot, Themes, session-log download), the Nord/Monokai/Hacker palettes, and the pack's appearance overrides - Markdown paper, the branding band, the account menu's Feedback row removed, and the right bar's resize seam. See packages/dsh-themes/README.md.
overrides: markdown paper: re-declares ui-theme's light declarations on the rendered Markdown root, so the page stays white in the dark theme
markdown chrome: hides the preview header's viewer menu on Markdown tabs (the page has exactly one renderer; the editor's Edit button is the way back to editing)

left top bar: the sidebar branding row becomes the 76px band the middle and right columns open with, its hairline at the same y=76 in both rail states, with the mark, brand name and collapse control on the band's top strip and the core's 8px/12px gap kept under the line; pinned to the sidebar's hashed class names

branding: the left bar brand row drops the shipped mark and wordmark - whatever occupies the single-occupant sidebar.brand.mark / sidebar.brand.name slots, including the layout fallback - and draws a 24px black disc plus the product text vncode in their place (alpha.14; the draw string read VN Harness through alpha.13), in the wide row and in the collapsed rail

branding type: the vncode text wears the conversation title's own type - 14px/20px at weight 500, the size of ui-conversation's current crumb - instead of the shipped brand name's 18px/600, which sat in the same 30px strip

branding mark: the drawn disc is replaced by the app icon itself - assets/vncode.svg at the pack root, a black circle centred on (12,12) with a 1px transparent margin inside its box - inlined as a data URI so no route or request is needed, and painted at 24px in the left bar (wide row and rail) and 26px in the empty conversation hero, where the shipped whale is also hidden

header ring: the right bar's own collapse/expand toggle in the header corner wears the same .5px round hairline outline as this package's own header icon buttons, keyed on the header's stable data-conversation-header-corner marker rather than a hashed class

session-log download seat: the shipped @deepseek-ai/dsh-session-log-export browser half's three-dot button - whose one menu item was Download session log - is shadowed by registering the SAME occupant id (session-log-download) at priority -10, which is a list slot's own lowest-renders rule, so the seat draws one plain download icon button that starts the export on the first click; nothing shipped is disabled, because that row owns the host half (/api/session.export and the /export command) and publishes the sessionLogDownload controller this button drives, and the seat's preparing/success/error dialog is rendered here from that same store so /export keeps its feedback

capture rule: for the one frame the Screenshot control grabs, html[data-dsh-screenshot] hides the OPEN TOOLTIP BUBBLE (keyed on the shipped Tooltip's own role="tooltip" marker, never a hashed class) and nothing else - since alpha.11 the picture is the interface as it stands, this package's header controls included, because a shot that dropped the buttons that took it was a hole in the record; the clicked button also passes disabled to its own Tooltip while the capture runs, so its hover card is closed rather than merely hidden

page zoom: one inline `zoom` on <html> - removed again at 100% - along Chrome's own zoom ladder (50% to 200%, cut at 200% for the reason recorded with the ladder: the control is inside the page it zooms, and a browser zoom reflows the shell, so a rung past that puts the header's utilities row outside the shrunken layout viewport). The menu keeps itself open over a step, like the browser's own zoom submenu, and closes on a pointer press outside it or on Escape (the shipped Menu's own behaviour); the button carries the level in `data-dsh-page-zoom` and in its tooltip, and the level is remembered per origin in localStorage (`dsh-themes.page-zoom`) and re-applied before the control's first render

right bar seam under a zoom: the frame places the right bar's outer resize seam with `left: viewport - rightbar`, where `viewport` is the SCALED `getBoundingClientRect().width` a root zoom produces while `left` is layout pixels - so with a level in force the seam slid off the right column's edge (288px at 80% on a 1440px frame) and the bar could no longer be dragged, which in the desktop window (the one host the control exists for) reads as 'the right bar stops being resizable after I zoom'; the LEFT bar's seam was never affected, its `left` being a layout-pixel width with no measurement folded into it. Fixed rather than documented (alpha.16): two rules, gated on `html[data-dsh-page-zoomed]` - the marker `applyZoom` writes beside the declaration it belongs to, so they are inert at 100% and the frame's own inline `left` still governs - name the right column as a CSS anchor on ui-layout's own stable `data-rightbar-col` marker (the one dsh-terminal already follows) and set the seam to `anchor(--dsh-themes-rightbar-seam left) !important` on `[data-side="rightbar"]`, which is layout pixels on both sides. No fork, no core row disabled, nothing for sync-vendored.ps1; a browser without anchor positioning drops the declarations and leaves the behaviour of before. Measured in the desktop window at 80%, 100% and 125% with real pointer input: the seam sits on the column's edge to 0.00px and a drag still resizes the panel

account menu: the account menu's shipped **Feedback** row is HIDDEN (alpha.21), because vncode does not ask its users for feedback and that row is the only control in the app that opens an EXTERNAL form in a new window - @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-settings-account's contactUrl() builds it with the uid, the locale, the harness version, the screen size and the device info attached (the default is a Feishu questionnaire at trtgsjkv6r.feishu.cn). There is no row to disable: the item is hardcoded in that package's AccountMenu and registered into the settings.launcher slot whole, so the alternatives were a fork of 4.5k lines (sign-in, sign-out, quota notices, billing pages, onboarding) or one rule. The rule keys on the ICON - the paper-plane path data the row draws - rather than on a hashed class, since the primitive renders rows with no id or data attribute and the artwork outlives the class names a rebuild renames; it hides the row's wrapper AND its button (the primitive's shape today and the bare-button fallback), and it is scoped to `[role="menu"]` so the same artwork drawn by the chat's turn-trigger notice and by the Session-export header button is untouched. Hiding is enough: a display:none row cannot take focus or be clicked, while the Menu's keyboard walk still advances past it, so Settings and Sign out stay reachable. Accepted failure mode, the same one the top-bar and branding pins carry: a future harness that redraws the artwork makes the rule match nothing and the item returns - and a `config` override of contactFormUrl was rejected because a row with `volatile` fields loses its whole config on the next volatile write. No fork, no core row disabled, nothing for sync-vendored.ps1

theme extensions: the Themes control's menu is the SHIPPED registry's own list (snapshot.themes, with the system preference last), and this package registers its palettes into it through ctx.theme.register - ui-theme's documented third-party surface, whose alias-token overrides ui-layout writes as inline body variables over the base palette colorScheme selects. The first registered theme is Nord (alpha.12): the Nord palette's Polar Night surfaces (nord0 page and sidebar alike), Snow Storm text, Frost accents and Aurora states as 93 token overrides (73 alias, 11 specific, 9 shiki) on the DARK base. Monokai follows it (alpha.13), in the same 93-token shape on the DARK base: the classic TextMate palette's near-black warm page (#272822), off-white body (#f8f8f2), pink keywords (#f92672) as the brand, cyan types (#66d9ef) as links and the info state, yellow strings, green functions, orange parameters and purple constants in the syntax tokens, the theme's line highlight and selection as the surface steps, and the olive comment grey (#75715e) as the quietest text tier. Hacker follows Monokai (alpha.19), again in the same 93-token shape on the DARK base: the phosphor terminal, with a near-black green-cast page (#0a0e0a) shared by the conversation and the sidebar, the phosphor body (#d8ffe0), the signal green (#00ff41) as the brand, success and primary button, amber (#ffb000) for warnings and strings, cyan (#00d9ff) for links and the info state, a plain red for errors, and the dim green (#3f6b4a) as the quietest text tier and the comment token - with every hover and pressed step DERIVED from the palette's own colours by the arithmetic Monokai documents rather than invented. The header button wears one static appearance mark instead of the active preference's sun/moon, and the theme stays in-process because the durable preference schema accepts light/dark/system only. Adding a theme is one entry in THEME_EXTENSIONS plus its theme.<id> copy in both dictionaries and its own menu glyph

dsh-canvas.role: Canvas: a design page the agent drives - eleven `canvas_*` tools over a small JSON design language validated on the host and painted by the browser, exported at preset sizes, with a style library, presets, archetypes, an asset store and a vendored Excalidraw surface. See packages/dsh-canvas/README.md.
vendors: Inter 400/600/700 + Space Grotesk 500/700 Latin WOFF2 subsets, and Excalidraw 0.18.1 + React 18.3.1 as a classic script with its stylesheet and 25 Latin faces (lib/vendor/, GENERATED by vendor/build.mjs; VERSION.json records a sha256 per file, the trims and the repository patches, and --check re-hashes it offline). The build's first patch, `firebase-api-key-redacted`, blanks the api key Excalidraw ships in its own OSS Firebase literal.
the canvas-design and social-banners skills, copied into $DSH_HOME/skills by both installers
